SHBUI headphone surround impulse responses

Bill Gardner and Keith Martin, HRTF Measurements of a KEMAR Dummy-Head
Microphone, MIT Media Lab, May 1994 (Technical Report 280).
Copyright 1994 by the MIT Media Laboratory.
The authors permit use of the data, including in commercial applications,
subject to attribution. Their terms and measurements are available at
https://sound.media.mit.edu/resources/KEMAR.html
https://sound.media.mit.edu/resources/KEMAR/hrtfdoc.txt

Source: https://sound.media.mit.edu/resources/KEMAR/compact.zip
SHA-256: 0bcd69f8e8760cf8eacff4a89594ceca7d44fb94f28ecf0bf19970003bbfb3e0

The compact set derives symmetric 128-sample binaural responses from the
small-pinna measurements and includes loudspeaker equalization. SHBUI uses
five horizontal source directions, 15, 30, 45, 60 and 75 degrees. SHBUI
separates the near/far channels, mirrors the source pair, converts to
little-endian float32 and supplies an impulse-gain-corrected 48 kHz copy.
All directions share one attenuation for headroom. The transformation is
reproducible with scripts/generate-kemar-responses.py.
